rationales.wacc: Judgment, CAPM-based. Cost of equity = risk-free rate of about 4.25% + beta of about 1.3 x equity risk premium of 5.0%, which gives about 10.75%. The beta and the 5.0% ERP are analyst assumptions: the case snapshot has no index or rate series, so neither can be estimated from data here, and the 4.25% risk-free rate is an assumption, not a sourced figure. Beta is set above 1 because NVDA's revenue depends on hyperscaler and AI-infrastructure capex, which is cyclical; it is set below the roughly 1.7 to 2.0 a high-volatility semi might show because NVDA is now a mega-cap. Debt is LongTermDebt $33.366B (F-de060525b4) against a market value of equity of about $5.05T (24,100M cover-page shares x $209.66 close on 2026-08-26), so debt weight is under 1% and after-tax cost of debt barely moves the result: WACC is about 10.7%, rounded to 10.5%. Sensitivity (code inputs otherwise unchanged, rough offline check): 10.0% raises DCF value per share by about 7%, 12.0% lowers it by about 17%.
rationales.terminal_growth: 3.0%: long-run nominal growth roughly in line with global nominal GDP plus a small premium for secular growth in compute demand. That is well below WACC (10.5%) and inside the gate bound of [0, 4%]. We do not use a higher rate because the explicit period already ends with growth fading to 5%, and AI-infrastructure spending carries real cyclical and competitive risk (custom accelerators at AVGO and MRVL, GPUs at AMD).
rationales.revenue_growth: Years 2-5 apply to code's NTM revenue, which comes from assumptions.json: four quarters from FY2027Q3 to FY2028Q2, about $492B; FY2027Q3 is anchored on the $108.0B guide (Q-1). The exit run-rate of FY2028Q2 (about $137B x 4 = about $549B) is already about 11.5% above NTM with no further sequential growth, so year 2 at 15% assumes only modest sequential growth continues. After that, growth fades to 10%, 7% and 5% as the AI build-out matures and competition rises. No China Data Center compute revenue is assumed (Q-2). This is judgment; no guidance exists beyond FY2027Q3.
rationales.fcf_margin: Margins are grounded in history, measured as CFO (NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities) minus capex (PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets), relative to Revenues, using the year-to-date XBRL facts. FY2024: (28.090-1.069)/60.922 = 44.4% (F-c6d18e3588, F-9442a91323, F-a650c0b6ab, as re-reported in the FY2026 10-K). FY2025: (64.089-3.236)/130.497 = 46.6% (F-0895726b1c, F-3eba3b27d5, F-053ca36afd). FY2026: (102.718-6.042)/215.938 = 44.8% (F-48ea7477fe, F-b12a70d09b, F-d514650a55). H1 FY2027: (74.421-4.434)/177.837 = 39.4% (F-e325572968, F-2b25fa17c5, F-f21b6e99e6). TTM to 2026-07-26: (102.718-42.779+74.421)-(6.042-3.122+4.434) over (215.938-90.805+177.837) = 127.0/303.0 = 41.9% (H1 FY2026 comparatives F-fb481caf7b, F-38691604f8, F-b869ccf9b6). The H1 FY2027 shortfall comes from working capital. The 10-Q cash flow statement shows accounts receivable -24.6B (from extended payment terms on large multi-quarter agreements, per MD&A), inventories -10.2B and prepaid/other -6.5B, partly offset by payables and accruals. Commitments rose to $279B, mainly for memory procurement (Q-10). Year 1 is set at 42%, close to TTM, because we assume this drag continues for a while. Years 2-3 are set at 44%, near the three-year full-year average of about 45%, as revenue growth slows and working-capital investment eases. Years 4-5 fade to 43% and 42% for competitive pressure on gross margin, which is 74% guided (Q-3) versus about 75% recently. CFO already adds back stock-based compensation (H1 FY2027 $3.954B, about 2% of revenue), so these margins are before SBC; dilution is reflected only through the share count. CFO also excludes the $23.7B of H1 gains on equity securities that sit in net income, which is why we use CFO-based FCF and not earnings.
rationales.peers: AMD, AVGO and MRVL, all from config/project.yaml coverage. AMD is the direct merchant GPU/accelerator competitor. AVGO (custom AI accelerators/XPUs plus Ethernet data-center networking) and MRVL (custom AI silicon and data-center interconnect) compete for the same hyperscaler AI-infrastructure budgets. Excluded: INTC (CPU/foundry turnaround with negative TTM earnings; not comparable on margins or growth); MU (memory, a commodity price cycle; NVDA is its customer); AMAT, LRCX and KLAC (wafer-fab equipment, a different end market); SNPS and CDNS (EDA software); ALAB, CRDO and MPWR (connectivity and power-component suppliers with TTM revenue of $1-3B, too small and too high-multiple, about 20-42x EV/Sales, to be fair EV/Sales comparators for a company with about $300B of revenue). In a rough offline check using the snapshot, TTM EV/Sales was AMD about 18.9x, AVGO about 23.0x and MRVL about 24.7x, so the median is about 23.0x. NVDA itself trades at about 16.7x on TTM revenue of about $303B. Peer TTM windows end May-June 2026, compared with July 2026 for NVDA.
rationales.dcf_weight: 0.7 on the DCF and 0.3 on peer EV/Sales. The DCF captures NVDA-specific economics (FCF margins of about 42-46% grounded in history, guided gross margin) that EV/Sales ignores. The peer set is small (three) and its multiples rest on much lower-margin earnings bases: TTM P/E is about 122x for AMD, 145x for AVGO and 85x for MRVL, so applying peer EV/Sales to NVDA revenue mixes margin structures that do not match. We keep a 30% weight on peers so the target reflects how the market currently prices AI-semiconductor revenue; the DCF terminal value is about 72% of EV, below 80%, so the DCF is not dominated by the terminal value.
rationales.net_cash: Code computes net cash as mapped cash + short_term_investments - total_debt = 22.443B (F-65cf7ca5f8) + 0 (short_term_investments unmapped) - 33.366B (F-de060525b4) = -10.923B. That leaves out material liquid assets on the 2026-07-26 balance sheet (periodic.txt line 263 and the fair-value table near line 790). First, marketable debt securities of $34.143B: $33.003B is US Treasury and $1.140B is US government agency debt, so they are effectively cash. Second, marketable equity securities of $42.783B: these are publicly held equities, non-operating but price-volatile, and $36.9B of NVDA's publicly held equity investments are under short-term lock-up restrictions on sale (periodic.txt footnote 1). No XBRL concept in the snapshot carries either line; MarketableSecuritiesCurrent stops at 2025-10-26, so gen-mapping left short_term_investments null. In our judgment the marketable debt securities belong in net cash. The marketable equity securities could be added after a haircut for volatility and the lock-ups. Non-marketable securities ($51.157B) should stay out. On 24,285M diluted shares, the per-share effect is about +$1.41 with the debt securities and about +$3.17 with both lines. We flag this for the lead to route to gen-mapping or the controller code. We did not change the inputs above to compensate.
